source_text:
Ἔστιν οὖν γαστριμαργία, πορνείας μήτηρ, τροφὸς λογισμῶν,
νηστείας ἀτονία, ἀσκήσεως φίμωτρον, στοχασμοῦ φόβητρον, ἐξεικονισμὸς βρωμάτων, σκιαγράφος ἀρτυμάτων, ἀνειμένος πῶλος, ἀχαλίνωτος μανία, δοχεῖον νόσου, ὑγείας φθόνος, φραγμὸς συρίγγων, στεναγμὸς ἐντέρων, ὕβρεων πέρας, πορνείας σύμμιστος, διανοίας ῥύπος, σώματος ἀσθένεια, φορτικὸς ὕπνος, ἀμειδὴς θάνατος. Ἐγκράτεια, γαστρὸς χαλινὸς, ἀπληστείας δὲ μάστιξ, συμμετρίας δὲ σταθμὸς, ἀδηφαγίας δὲ κημὸς, ἀναπαύσεως ἀποταγὴ, σκληρουχίας συνταγὴ, λογισμῶν δαμαστήριον ἀγρυπνίας ὄμμα, πυρώσεως ῥύσις, σώματος παιδαγωγὸς, πόνων πύργος, καὶ τρόπων τεῖχος, ἠθῶν καταστολὴ, καὶ παθῶν ἀναστολὴ, νέκρωσις μελῶν, ἀναβίωσις ψυχῶν, ἀναστάσεως μίμημα, ἁγιασμοῦ πολίτευμα. Πορνεία, λαιμαργίας κύημα, προμαλακτὴρ καρδίας, πυρώσεως κάμινος, νυμφαγωγὸς εἰδώλων, ἀσυγγενὴς πρᾶξις, σκιαζομένη μορφὴ, φανταζομένη συμπλοκὴ, ἐνυπνίων κλίνη, ἀναίσθητος συνουσία, ὀφθαλμῶν δόλος, βλέμματος ἀναίδεια, εὐχῆς ἐντροπὴ, καρδίας αἰσχύνη, ἀγνωσίας ὁδηγός. Σωφροσύνη, ἀληθείας στολὴ, ἀσελγείας πέλυξ, ὀφθαλμῶν ἡνίοχος, ἐπίσκοπος λογισμῶν, ἐννοίας περιτομὴ, ἀκολασίας δὲ ἐκτομὴ, φύσεως ἀντίφυτος, καὶ πυρώσεως ἀντίθετος, ἔργων ἐπεργὸς, καὶ ἐγκρατείας συνεργὸς, καρδίας λαμπτὴρ, εὐχῆς γνώμων. 1 ΚΕΦΑΛ. Γʹ. Φιλαργυρία εἰδώλων φειδωλεῖον, δήμου προφητεία, σφιγγίας ψῆφος, ἐναποθέτων λογιστεία, αἰχμαλωσίας πλοῦτος, ἀδικίας γένος, νοσημάτων πιότης, πολυετίας μάντις, φιλεργίας ἐπῳδὸς, ἀγρυπνίας σύμβουλος, γαστρὸς πενία, βρωμάτων εὐτέλεια, ἀκόρεστος μανία. πολυμέριμνος κακία.
thought_title: Gluttony, Sexual Immorality and Love of Money with Their Opposites
orientation: Evagrius now begins his paired list of vices and virtues with gluttony, sexual immorality and love of money.
pass_a_gloss: Gluttony is therefore mother of sexual immorality, rearer of thoughts, weakness of fasting, muzzle of training, frightener of reflection, portrayal of foods, painter in shadow of seasonings, colt let loose, madness without bridle, vessel of disease, grudging of health, blocking of channels, groaning of intestines, end of outrages, thing mixed together with sexual immorality, filth of mind, weakness of body, burdensome sleep, death without smile. Self control is bridle of stomach, and whip of unsatisfied desire, and standard of due measure, and muzzle of ravenous eating, renunciation of rest, compact of hardship, tamer of thoughts, eye of wakefulness, rescue from burning, trainer of body, tower of labors, and wall of habits, settling of character, and checking of passions, deadening of limbs, reviving of souls, imitation of resurrection, citizenship of sanctification. Sexual immorality is offspring of greed of the throat, softener of heart beforehand, furnace of burning, conductor of images to marriage, act without kin, form shaded in darkness, embrace seen in fantasy, bed of dreams, intercourse without perception, trick of eyes, shamelessness of glance, shame of prayer, disgrace of heart, guide of ignorance. Chastity is clothing of truth, axe of wantonness, driver of eyes, overseer of thoughts, cutting around of intention, and cutting out of wantonness, plant set against nature, and thing set against burning, worker of works, and worker together with self control, lamp of heart, interpreter of prayer. Chapter 3. Love of money is storehouse of idols, prophecy of the people, pebble of the sphinx, reckoning of deposits, wealth of captivity, offspring of injustice, fatness of diseases, foreteller of many years, chant of love of work, adviser of wakefulness, poverty of stomach, plainness of foods, madness that cannot be sated. Evil rich in cares.

choices.why: genitive of sphinx as riddle creature, not strangling, with pebble for vote
participle means let go or released, image of lack of control

pass_b_english: Gluttony is the mother of sexual immorality. It feeds anxious thoughts and leaves fasting feeble. It muzzles ascetic practice and scares disciplined reflection away. It pictures dishes vividly and traces seasonings in shadow. It is a colt let loose and a madness without a bridle. It is a vessel of sickness and the envy of health. It blocks the passages, makes the bowels groan, and brings insult to its limit. It is the close companion of sexual immorality, the filth of the mind, and the sickness of the body. It brings burdensome sleep and a joyless death.

Self-control is the bridle of the stomach. It is the whip for insatiability, the standard for proportion, and the muzzle for voracious eating. It renounces ease and pledges itself to hard living. It tames thoughts and keeps its eye on wakefulness. It rescues from burning desire, trains the body, and stands as a tower in toils and a wall around conduct. It orders character and holds the passions back. It puts the limbs to death so souls may live again. It imitates the resurrection and lives the life of sanctification.

Sexual immorality is the offspring of greedy craving for food. It softens the heart and burns like a furnace. It leads idols to the bridal chamber and is an unnatural deed. It is a darkened face and an imagined embrace. It makes its bed in dreams and joins bodies without feeling. It cheats through the eyes and stares without shame. It brings shame into prayer and disgrace into the heart. It leads its followers into ignorance.

Chastity is the robe of truth. It is the axe laid to licentiousness, the charioteer of the eyes, and the overseer of thoughts. It cuts intention clean and cuts intemperance out. It grows against nature and stands against burning desire. It completes good works and labors alongside self-control. It is the lamp of the heart and the sure measure of prayer.

Love of money is the storehouse of idols. It prophesies to the crowd and is the reckoning of stinginess. It keeps strict account of deposits and grows rich into captivity. It breeds injustice and fattens diseases. It foretells long life, chants over love of labor, and counsels sleeplessness. It starves the stomach while praising cheap food. It is an insatiable madness and an evil full of many cares.
notes: final clause πολυμέριμνος κακία stands after a full stop as a separate nominal phrase in the given source
chapter heading ΚΕΦΑΛ Γ glossed as Chapter 3

problems.quote: casts the pebble of the sphinx
problems.why: σφιγγία means stinginess or tight-fistedness, not the Sphinx (Σφίγξ), and ψῆφος here means reckoning or counting.
problems.ruling: σφιγγία is stinginess, not Σφίγξ; ψῆφος is reckoning, not casting sphinx's pebble

problems.quote: acts as a stranger to kin
problems.why: Misreads the noun πρᾶξις (deed, act) as the verb 'acts'; the Greek means an unnatural or alien deed.
problems.ruling: ἀσυγγενὴς πρᾶξις is noun phrase: alien/unrelated deed, not verb acts

edits.old: casts the pebble of the sphinx
acts as a stranger to kin

fixed: σφιγγίας ψῆφος: corrected Sphinx/pebble to stinginess/reckoning
ἀσυγγενὴς πρᾶξις: corrected verb-phrase misreading to noun phrase unnatural deed

last_rejected.why: In English 'the envy of health' means health envies gluttony, reversing the Greek objective genitive (begrudging or spoiling health).
last_rejected.ruling: ὑγείας φθόνος: objective genitive; English “envy of health” normally means envy toward health, not health envying.
